**The literal: `"2026-12-25T07:00:00"` at `src/date.ts:29`**, inside `christmasMorning()`. Flagged as `crime_00012` (`timezone_unsafe_parse`, "Timezone Roulette", medium/0.9).

## Why it's the one

The finding names two literals, but only one of them can produce a CI-vs-prod split:

| Line | Literal | How V8 parses it | Host-dependent? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 29 | `"2026-12-25T07:00:00"` | date**-time** with no offset → **local time** | **yes** |
| 33 | `"2026-12-20"` | date-**only** → **UTC midnight** (ECMA-262) | no |

The date-only form at line 33 resolves to the same instant on every machine, so it can't be the cause of a test that passes in CI and fails in production. The unzoned date-time at line 29 is the only parse in the file whose resulting instant moves with `TZ`:

- CI, `TZ=UTC` → `2026-12-25T07:00:00Z`
- Prod, `TZ=Europe/Berlin` (CET, UTC+1) → `2026-12-25T06:00:00Z`

Europe is *ahead* of UTC, so the same wall-clock literal resolves to an **earlier absolute instant** — the boundary trips sooner for European users, which is the direction of the reported bug. One caveat on magnitude: the shift is 1h in winter (2h under CEST), so it flips a *calendar day* only where the boundary is bucketed to a day downstream — which this file does elsewhere (`crime_00010`, "Half-UTC, Half-Local" on `src/date.ts:9,41`). If you want the day-flip mechanism nailed down rather than just the hour drift, that's where to look next.

## Smallest change

Append the explicit UTC designator. One character, same function name, same signature, same return type:

```diff
 export function christmasMorning(): Date {
-  return new Date("2026-12-25T07:00:00");
+  return new Date("2026-12-25T07:00:00Z");
 }
```

Production now parses to `2026-12-25T07:00:00Z` on every host — exactly what CI has been asserting all along. This is `crime_00012`'s own `fix_timezone_parse` action, risk `low`.

Two optional follow-ups, deliberately kept out of the minimal fix:

- `"2026-12-20"` → `"2026-12-20T00:00:00Z"` is **behaviour-neutral** (it already means UTC midnight) but makes the intent legible and stops the next reader from "fixing" it in the wrong direction. It also removes the trap for users *behind* UTC if anything ever renders that date with local getters.
- Add a regression test pinned to `TZ=Europe/Berlin`. A UTC-only CI matrix is what let this ship — the current test can't fail on this class of bug no matter how the parse behaves.

Not touching the DST arithmetic at line 52 (`crime_00018`, `+ 86400000`) or the mixed UTC/local reads at line 41 — real findings, but neither is the parse-time bug you asked about, and folding them in would make this more than the smallest change.

I did not edit the file — this fixture is intentionally-bad eval input, so changing it would move the baseline for other scenarios.
